light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

The place is a real, messy home garage-workshop of a working-class house in Latin America: concrete floor with old stains and cement dust, a wooden workbench covered in tools, tins, rags and offcuts, a pegboard with hanging tools, stacked plastic buckets, a bicycle leaning on the wall, bare painted brick walls with damp patches, the wide garage door on the left open to the street. He is the man of the reference photo — same face, same dark curly hair, same short salt-and-pepper beard — wearing a faded olive-green work shirt with the sleeves rolled up to the elbows, stained with paint and dust, and a worn brown leather apron over it. At the workbench: one half of an old white porcelain toilet sawn in half lengthwise: the flat cut face shows the inside of the curved trap channel lined with a thick, rough, layered crust of yellow-brown and grey limescale, like stone, narrowing the passage to less than half, two clear drinking glasses side by side, a small saucepan, a bottle of clear white vinegar without label, a grey pumice stone, a small cup of water and a clean white offcut of porcelain. He stands behind the bench, waist-up, holding a small chunk of yellow-brown limescale crust between two gloved fingers, showing it to the camera. Light: flat overcast daylight coming in through the open garage door on the left, plus one plain fluorescent tube on the ceiling; the side near the door a little brighter and cooler, the back corners dimmer.

clips.text: Ahora, ¿por qué funciona el vinagre? Te lo muestro aquí mismo, con un pedazo de esta costra.
clips.action: He turns the chunk of crust in his gloved fingers and talks to the camera, then puts it down on the bench.

clips.text: Eso con vinagre no sale ni en un año.
clips.action: The neighbour looks at the glasses, waves his hand dismissively and says his line with a skeptical grin; the presenter listens.
clips.line: Eso con vinagre no sale ni en un año.
clips.who: the neighbour (the fourth reference image is his face)
clips.voice: the neighbour (the fourth reference image is his face), in Spanish with a neutral Latin American accent, the gruff, amused voice of a 65-year-old man; the presenter does NOT speak

clips.text: Vamos a ver. En este vaso, vinagre frío. En este otro, vinagre caliente. Mismo pedazo de costra en cada uno.
clips.action: He pours cold vinegar from the bottle into the left glass and hot vinegar from the small saucepan into the right glass, then drops one piece of crust into each, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Mira las burbujitas. Eso es el ácido del vinagre deshaciendo la cal. En el caliente salen más rápido, mucho más.
clips.action: Tiny bubbles rise from the pieces of crust, many more from the hot glass on the right.

clips.text: Por eso te dije caliente. Pero ojo: caliente, no hirviendo. Agua hirviendo en una loza fría puede rajarla.
clips.action: He points at the steaming glass, then raises a warning finger to the camera.

clips.text: Y otra prueba, la más importante. Este pedazo de loza, de la parte limpia, lo voy a frotar con la piedra pómez… seca.
clips.action: He picks up the clean white offcut of porcelain and the dry grey pumice stone and shows both to the camera.

clips.text: ¿Ves estas rayas grises? Eso es el esmalte rayado. Y un esmalte rayado junta sarro el doble de rápido. Por eso la piedra, siempre mojada.
clips.action: The dry pumice rubs a few times on the glossy porcelain and is lifted away, leaving dull grey scratches.

clips.text: Ahora, mojada. La misma piedra, la misma fuerza. Mira: la costra sale y el esmalte queda liso. El agua hace de colchón.
clips.action: The wet pumice rubs gently; the crust dissolves into grey mud and smooth glossy porcelain appears.

clips.text: Y el vinagre del vaso, después de una hora. La costra se ablandó por fuera. Por dentro sigue dura. Por eso lleva más de una pasada.
clips.action: He lifts a piece of crust out of the vinegar glass with his gloved fingers, presses it — the outside is soft and crumbles a little — and talks to the camera.

clips.text: Probé también con ácido cítrico en polvo, el de cocina, disuelto en agua caliente. Hizo lo mismo que el vinagre caliente, y sin el olor.
clips.action: He shows a small clear bag of white citric acid powder, then a glass with cloudy water beside it, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Lo que no hizo ninguno es deshacer la costra entera en un rato. Eso no existe. Lo que existe es tiempo, repetición y la piedra mojada.
clips.action: He puts everything down and talks to the camera, counting three things on his fingers.

clips.text: Y el vinagre no daña el esmalte sano. Lo que sí lo daña es frotar con algo duro: un cuchillo, una lija, un destornillador. Eso nunca.
clips.action: He picks up an old kitchen knife from the bench, shakes his head, puts it down far away, talking to the camera.
The neighbour peers at the bubbling glass, purses his lips and admits his line reluctantly, nodding a little.
